material_difference: Old interval_boundary_count_binding used 6 red midpoint dots versus 4 blue width-boundary dots to elicit a boundary/interval miscount. Its only complete final was C; run2 was aborted. This new design adds no dots and does not ask for four width intervals. It binds all THREE actual brick axes to parallel WHOLE-CUBE edges, targeting the different error of transferring repeat counts directly into brick side lengths instead of inversely. The new wrong rationale is the true counts depth:width:height=2:3:6, scaled directly so minimum2 becomes4, giving4:6:12=A. This is not the old observed C plus cosmetics, or a retry of the aborted image. Same target letter A arises from a different predeclared operation.
predeclared_wrong_hypothesis: Match three real unit edges to three parallel whole-cube edges; mistakenly use repeat counts2:3:6 as dimensions and scale to shortest4, yielding4x6x12, A.
primary_proof: All bricks are aligned in the actual source and frozen scene. The cube has 3 width columns, 2 depth strips and 6 height layers. Equal total edge lengths imply 3w=2d=6h=s. Hence h is shortest; h=4 gives s=24,w=8,d=12. The only listed dimensions are C:4x8x12. Color matches only axis direction and does not assert that a unit edge equals the full cube edge.
risks: Colors could help solve correctly rather than cause the targeted inversion; no effectiveness assumed.
